findings.claim: The explanation page is scoped as why audits only report, but the audit agent, its review skills and the opt-in LLM audit tier do not exist yet: plugin/ has no agents/, the tickets audit-agent-and-skills and ci-audit are still in planning, and the manifesto marks I2 as planned. A docs/ page about them breaks docs-describe-what-exists, the rule this ticket cites as its reason. Narrow the page to what is built (kmctl check, kmctl review due and the CI action report and never write; the hook is SessionStart only) or leave audits to the audit tickets.

The contract says every command on a page is run and its real output pasted, but the how-to's commands cannot be run that way as planned. kmctl plugin install calls the claude CLI, adds the scaccogatto/okf-skills marketplace over the network and writes the operator's Claude config and ~/.local/share/kmctl (src/kmctl/plugin.py), and the CI action only runs on GitHub. The plan needs to say how those steps are verified, for example a run with an isolated HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME, or a carve-out naming which output is quoted from tests or from --help. Whether a project-scope install can run in a scratch repository without touching the operator's config is a spike question.

The explanation page described audits that were not built. The plan now depends on audit-agent-and-skills and ci-audit, so the page is written after the audits exist. The dependency graph has no cycle (ci-audit depends on ci-action and audit-agent-and-skills; audit-agent-and-skills on claude-plugin and review-due).

Run-every-command could not cover plugin install or the CI action. The plan now names two exceptions: plugin install runs in a scratch repository with isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME, which tests/test_plugin_install.py already does successfully with a project-scope install, and GitHub-only steps are quoted from action.yml and the shipped workflow with the page saying so.
